Trauma-focused psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy for PTSD: a systematic review of comparative evidence.
This systematic review synthesized randomized trials comparing trauma-focused psychotherapies, including
prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy, with pharmacotherapy and combined treatment for
adults with post-traumatic stress disorder. Trauma-focused psychotherapy showed the largest and most
durable effect sizes and is recommended as first-line treatment in most clinical guidelines. Combined
treatment did not consistently outperform psychotherapy alone. The review discusses outcomes in comorbid
populations, including depression and chronic pain, and notes that many trials excluded patients with
active substance use or recent suicidal behaviour, limiting applicability to complex veteran presentations.
Recency, study quality, and population match should be weighed above citation count when selecting evidence.
